+# The Euclidean sphere cannot be contracted
+
+## Abstract
+
+The Euclidean sphere cannot be contracted.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Noncontractibility from reduced singular homology).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Topology/SphereBrouwerObstruction.not_contractible_unit_sphere`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Topology/SphereBrouwerObstruction.not_contractible_unit_sphere` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* David V. Feldman and Alexander Wilce (2026). *A Note on Compactness and Clique Size, Question 3*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13320v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every positive natural n, the unit sphere of real Euclidean n-space is not contractible. Ambient dimension one is included.
+
+TauCeti computes the sphere's reduced singular homology with integer coefficients in degree n-1 and identifies it with the nonzero integer coefficient module. The upstream proof transports this computation from a Euclidean space of the same dimension, so its statement applies to every nontrivial finite-dimensional real normed space.
+
+A contraction would make reduced singular homology zero in every degree. The sphere computation would then force the integer coefficient module to be zero, contradicting the fact that zero and one are distinct.
+
+The endpoint is adopted from the exact TauCeti.not_contractibleSpace_sphere declaration by a source port, because the supplier and receiving Mathlib pins differ. The immutable source revision and path, TauCeti copyright, complete Apache-2.0 license, modification notices and own-pinned-Mathlib retirement condition are recorded in the linked Library note and port sources. The homology obstruction and lower-six result carry no novelty claim.
+
+## References
+
+- Truth anchor: `D5/S3/Topology/SphereBrouwerObstruction.not_contractible_unit_sphere`

+# Open orthogonality-free sphere covers
+
+## Abstract
+
+Relatively open orthogonality-free covers of the real two-sphere need at least six sets.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Orthogonality-free sets).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.OrthogonalityFree`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.OrthogonalityFree` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* David V. Feldman and Alexander Wilce (2026). *A Note on Compactness and Clique Size, Question 3*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13320v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For an arbitrary real inner product space E and a subset U of its unit sphere, OrthogonalityFree U means that every two points x and y in U have nonzero real inner product. The topology used for openness is the sphere's relative topology.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (Components are acute).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.component_inner_pos`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.component_inner_pos` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* David V. Feldman and Alexander Wilce (2026). *A Note on Compactness and Clique Size, Question 3*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13320v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+In a real inner product space, every actual connected component of an orthogonality-free subset of the unit sphere has strictly positive inner products between all its points.
+
+Fix one point x of the component. The continuous function taking y to its inner product with x never vanishes there and is positive at x. Connectedness forces it to remain positive throughout the component.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (Color multiplicity).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.cover_color_multiplicity`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.cover_color_multiplicity` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* David V. Feldman and Alexander Wilce (2026). *A Note on Compactness and Clique Size, Question 3*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13320v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+In ambient dimension n+1, a finite orthogonality-free cover with k colors has, at every unit vector x, at most k-n colors containing x. Openness is unnecessary for this counting statement.
+
+Take an orthonormal basis of the perpendicular space to x. Its n vectors require distinct colors, and none of these colors contains x. Counting these absent colors gives the bound.
+
+**Theorem 1.4 (Finite acute refinement).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.exists_finite_acute_refinement`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.exists_finite_acute_refinement` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* David V. Feldman and Alexander Wilce (2026). *A Note on Compactness and Clique Size, Question 3*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13320v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+On a compact locally connected unit sphere, a finite open orthogonality-free cover has a finite refinement by nonempty acute actual components whose multiplicity at each point is no greater than the original color multiplicity.
+
+Index a component by its original color and its actual subset, so that equal components of one color occur only once. Components are open, cover the sphere, and have a finite subcover by compactness. At any point the projection from selected containing components to original colors is injective, since two components of one open set that meet are equal.
+
+**Theorem 1.5 (The normalized cover map).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.acute_cover_normalized_map`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.acute_cover_normalized_map` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* David V. Feldman and Alexander Wilce (2026). *A Note on Compactness and Clique Size, Question 3*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13320v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For a finite open acute cover with a chosen representative in each member, there is a continuous sphere self-map homotopic to the identity. Its value at x lies in the linear span of representatives of cover members containing x.
+
+Choose a subordinate partition of unity and form F(x) as the weighted sum of the representatives. Each nonzero summand has positive inner product with x, so the inner product of x with F(x) is positive. In particular F(x) is nonzero. Normalize F, and normalize the straight segment from x to F(x) to obtain the homotopy. Zero coefficients remove all representatives whose cover members do not contain x.
+
+**Theorem 1.6 (Small spans omit a point).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.map_omits_point_of_small_spans`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.map_omits_point_of_small_spans` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* David V. Feldman and Alexander Wilce (2026). *A Note on Compactness and Clique Size, Question 3*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13320v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+In a positive finite dimensional real inner product space, a sphere map supported at each point on fewer representatives than the ambient dimension omits some sphere point.
+
+There are finitely many possible subsets of the finite representative family. The span of each subset smaller than the dimension is proper. A finite union of proper real subspaces misses a vector; normalizing that vector gives a point omitted by the sphere map.
+
+**Theorem 1.7 (The acute multiplicity obstruction).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.acute_cover_contractible_of_multiplicity_lt`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.acute_cover_contractible_of_multiplicity_lt` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* David V. Feldman and Alexander Wilce (2026). *A Note on Compactness and Clique Size, Question 3*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13320v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A finite open acute cover with multiplicities strictly smaller than the positive ambient dimension would make the sphere contractible.
+
+The normalized cover map is homotopic to the identity and omits a point. Stereographic projection identifies the punctured sphere with a real vector space, which is contractible. The map is therefore nullhomotopic, so the identity is nullhomotopic as well.
+
+**Theorem 1.8 (The original color multiplicity obstruction).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.open_cover_contractible_of_multiplicity_lt`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.open_cover_contractible_of_multiplicity_lt` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* David V. Feldman and Alexander Wilce (2026). *A Note on Compactness and Clique Size, Question 3*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13320v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+In ambient dimension n+1, a relatively open orthogonality-free cover whose original point multiplicities are below n+1 makes the sphere contractible.
+
+Pass to the finite acute component refinement, which preserves the original color multiplicity. Apply the normalized-map and omitted-point obstruction.
+
+**Theorem 1.9 (Too few colors force a contraction).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.low_color_cover_contractible`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.low_color_cover_contractible` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* David V. Feldman and Alexander Wilce (2026). *A Note on Compactness and Clique Size, Question 3*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13320v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+In ambient dimension n+1, an open orthogonality-free cover by at most 2n sets would make the sphere contractible. No component, acuteness, refinement or multiplicity hypothesis is assumed here.
+
+The orthogonal-complement count bounds every original color multiplicity by n. Finite refinement by actual acute components preserves this bound. Since n is smaller than the ambient dimension n+1, the acute multiplicity obstruction applies.
+
+**Theorem 1.10 (The general lower bound).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.sphere_open_orthogonality_free_cover_lower_bound`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.sphere_open_orthogonality_free_cover_lower_bound` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* David V. Feldman and Alexander Wilce (2026). *A Note on Compactness and Clique Size, Question 3*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13320v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every natural n at least two and every finite family of relatively open subsets of the real unit sphere in n dimensions, if the family covers the sphere and no member contains an orthogonal pair, then its size k satisfies 2n-1 at most k. Neither connectedness of the cover members nor any noncontractibility premise is required.
+
+If k were at most 2n-2, the preceding construction would contract the sphere. The source-ported TauCeti reduced singular homology obstruction rules this out: the sphere has nonzero reduced homology with integer coefficients in degree n-1, whereas a contractible space has zero reduced homology in every degree. This general lower estimate and the normalized weighted-sum mechanism are antecedents of Blondal, Hatami, Hatami, Lalov and Tretiak, arXiv:2606.06148v1, Theorem 2.1 (COLT 2026, Theorem 2). Here the dimension-two case is consumed by the perpendicular-circle step of the lower bound six. No priority or novelty claim is made.
+
+**Theorem 1.11 (Three colors absent at each point).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.sphere_three_absent_colors`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.sphere_three_absent_colors` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* David V. Feldman and Alexander Wilce (2026). *A Note on Compactness and Clique Size, Question 3*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13320v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every relatively open orthogonality-free finite cover of the real two-sphere and every unit vector x, at least three original colors omit x.
+
+Use an orthonormal basis of the perpendicular plane to identify its unit circle isometrically with the real unit circle. A color containing x has no point on this perpendicular circle. Restrict the remaining colors along the continuous isometry; they remain relatively open and orthogonality-free and cover the circle. The dimension-two general lower bound requires at least three such colors.
+
+**Theorem 1.12 (The lower bound six).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.sphere_two_open_orthogonality_free_cover_lower_six`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Topology/SphereOrthogonalityCover.sphere_two_open_orthogonality_free_cover_lower_six` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Citation.* David V. Feldman and Alexander Wilce (2026). *A Note on Compactness and Clique Size, Question 3*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13320v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Every finite relatively open orthogonality-free cover of the unit sphere in real Euclidean three-space has at least six members. Cover members may overlap and need not be connected.
+
+Assume at most five colors. At every sphere point the perpendicular-circle result excludes at least three colors, leaving multiplicity at most two. The original-color multiplicity obstruction contracts the two-sphere, contradicting the source-ported TauCeti reduced singular homology obstruction. The exact triangular lower bound is a known consequence of Proposition 4.1 in the OpenAI September 23 manuscript and its Lean Admissible.label_bound; this proof uses a topological cover construction and claims no new mathematical priority. Together with a matching six-set cover this lower bound gives the exact value six.
+
+## References
+

+/-- A set of unit vectors contains no orthogonal pair. -/
+def OrthogonalityFree (U : Set (sphere (0 : E) 1)) : Prop :=
+  ∀ x ∈ U, ∀ y ∈ U, ⟪(x : E), (y : E)⟫_ℝ ≠ 0

+/-- Every actual connected component of an orthogonality-free set of unit vectors is acute. -/
+theorem component_inner_pos {U : Set (sphere (0 : E) 1)} (hU : OrthogonalityFree U)
+    {a x y : sphere (0 : E) 1}
+    (hx : x ∈ connectedComponentIn U a) (hy : y ∈ connectedComponentIn U a) :
+    0 < ⟪(x : E), (y : E)⟫_ℝ := by
+  apply isPreconnected_connectedComponentIn.lt_of_ne
+    ((continuous_const.inner continuous_subtype_val).continuousOn)
+    (fun z hz => hU x (connectedComponentIn_subset U a hx) z
+      (connectedComponentIn_subset U a hz)) ?_ hy
+  refine ⟨x, hx, ?_⟩
+  rw [real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.mp x.property]
+  norm_num

+/-- Extending a unit vector by an orthonormal basis of its perpendicular space forces one
+distinct absent color per perpendicular direction. -/
+theorem cover_color_multiplicity {n k : ℕ} [Fact (finrank ℝ E = n + 1)]
+    (U : Fin k → Set (sphere (0 : E) 1))
+    (hcover : ∀ x, ∃ i, x ∈ U i) (hfree : ∀ i, OrthogonalityFree (U i))
+    (x : sphere (0 : E) 1) :
+    (Finset.univ.filter fun i => x ∈ U i).card + n ≤ k := by

+  let b := OrthonormalBasis.fromOrthogonalSpanSingleton (𝕜 := ℝ) n
+    (ne_zero_of_mem_unit_sphere x)

+    ⟨(b j : E), mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.mpr (b.orthonormal.norm_eq_one j)⟩
+  choose c hc using fun j => hcover (v j)
+  have hc_inj : Function.Injective c := by
+    intro i j hij
+    by_contra hne
+    apply hfree (c i) (v i) (hc i) (v j) (hij ▸ hc j)
+    exact b.orthonormal.inner_eq_zero hne

+    intro j hx
+    apply hfree (c j) x hx (v j) (hc j)
+    exact (Submodule.mem_orthogonal_singleton_iff_inner_right).mp (b j).property

+    calc
+      n = (Finset.univ.image c).card := by rw [Finset.card_image_of_injective _ hc_inj]; simp

+          obtain ⟨j, _, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hi
+          exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, hc_absent j⟩)

+    (p := fun i => x ∈ U i)
+  simp only [Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin] at hsum

+/-- A finite open orthogonality-free cover has a finite refinement by distinct actual

+      ∀ x, (t.filter fun j => x ∈ j.2).card ≤
+        (Finset.univ.filter fun i => x ∈ U i).card := by

+    ∃ a ∈ U j.1, j.2 = connectedComponentIn (U j.1) a}

+    obtain ⟨a, _, heq⟩ := j.property

+    obtain ⟨a, _, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hj

+      fun _ hx _ hy => component_inner_pos (hfree j.1) hx hy⟩

+      obtain ⟨b, hb, hlb⟩ := ht l hlt

+private def normalizeToSphere {Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace Y] (f : Y → E)
+    (hf : Continuous f) (h0 : ∀ y, f y ≠ 0) : C(Y, sphere (0 : E) 1) where

+    mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.mpr (NormedSpace.norm_normalize (h0 y))⟩

+/-- A finite acute open cover gives a sphere map homotopic to the identity. At each point
+its value lies in the span of the representatives of the sets containing that point. -/
+theorem acute_cover_normalized_map {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
+    (V : ι → Set (sphere (0 : E) 1)) (hopen : ∀ i, IsOpen (V i))
+    (hcover : ∀ x, ∃ i, x ∈ V i) (c : ι → sphere (0 : E) 1) (hc : ∀ i, c i ∈ V i)
+    (hacute : ∀ i, ∀ x ∈ V i, ∀ y ∈ V i, 0 < ⟪(x : E), (y : E)⟫_ℝ) :
+    ∃ g : C(sphere (0 : E) 1, sphere (0 : E) 1),
+      (ContinuousMap.id _).Homotopic g ∧
+      ∀ x, (g x : E) ∈ Submodule.span ℝ ((fun i => (c i : E)) '' {i | x ∈ V i}) := by
+  classical
+  obtain ⟨ψ, hψ⟩ := PartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate isClosed_univ V hopen
+    (fun x _ => mem_iUnion.mpr (hcover x))
+  have hsupport : ∀ i x, ψ i x ≠ 0 → x ∈ V i := by
+    intro i x hx
+    exact hψ i (subset_closure (show x ∈ Function.support (ψ i) from hx))
+  let F : sphere (0 : E) 1 → E := fun x => ∑ i, ψ i x • (c i : E)
+  have hF : Continuous F := by
+    exact continuous_finsetSum _ fun i _ => (ψ i).continuous.smul continuous_const
+  have hpos : ∀ x : sphere (0 : E) 1, 0 < ⟪(x : E), F x⟫_ℝ := by
+    intro x
+    change 0 < ⟪(x : E), ∑ i, ψ i x • (c i : E)⟫_ℝ
+    simp only [inner_sum, inner_smul_right]
+    apply Finset.sum_pos'
+    · intro i _
+      by_cases hi : ψ i x = 0
+      · simp [hi]
+      · exact mul_nonneg (ψ.nonneg i x) (hacute i x (hsupport i x hi) (c i) (hc i)).le
+    · obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := ψ.exists_pos (mem_univ x)

+        mul_pos hi (hacute i x (hsupport i x hi.ne') (c i) (hc i))⟩

+    have := hpos x

+/-- A sphere map supported pointwise on fewer representatives than the ambient dimension
+omits a point, since a finite union of proper linear subspaces cannot cover a real vector space. -/
+theorem map_omits_point_of_small_spans [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]

+    intro s
+    apply ne_of_lt
+    apply span_lt_top_of_ncard_lt_finrank (s.val.finite_toSet.image c)
+    exact lt_of_le_of_lt (by
+      simpa only [Finset.coe_sort_coe, Set.ncard_coe_finset] using
+        Set.ncard_image_le s.val.finite_toSet (f := c)) s.property
+  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := Submodule.exists_forall_notMem_of_forall_ne_top P hP
+  have hv0 : v ≠ 0 := by
+    intro hz
+    exact hv ⟨∅, by simpa using hdim⟩ (hz ▸ (P _).zero_mem)
+  let p : sphere (0 : E) 1 :=
+    ⟨NormedSpace.normalize v, mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.mpr (NormedSpace.norm_normalize hv0)⟩
+  refine ⟨p, ?_⟩
+  intro x hx
+  let s : A := ⟨Finset.univ.filter fun i => x ∈ V i, hcard x⟩
+  apply hv s
+  have hset : (s.val : Set ι) = {i | x ∈ V i} := by ext; simp [s]
+  change v ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (c '' (s.val : Set ι))
+  rw [hset]

+private theorem nullhomotopic_of_misses_point
+    (g : C(sphere (0 : E) 1, sphere (0 : E) 1))
+    (p : sphere (0 : E) 1) (hp : ∀ x, g x ≠ p) : g.Nullhomotopic := by
+  let e := stereographic (mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.mp p.property)
+  letI : ContractibleSpace e.target :=
+    (convex_univ : Convex ℝ (univ : Set (ℝ ∙ (p : E))ᗮ)).contractibleSpace univ_nonempty
+  letI : ContractibleSpace e.source := e.toHomeomorphSourceTarget.contractibleSpace
+  have hsource : ∀ x, g x ∈ e.source := by
+    intro x
+    simpa only [e, stereographic_source, mem_compl_iff, mem_singleton_iff] using hp x
+  let f : C(sphere (0 : E) 1, e.source) :=
+    ⟨fun x => ⟨g x, hsource x⟩, g.continuous.subtype_mk hsource⟩
+  let inclusion : C(e.source, sphere (0 : E) 1) := ⟨Subtype.val, continuous_subtype_val⟩

+open Classical in
+/-- An acute finite open cover with point multiplicities strictly below the ambient dimension
+would make the sphere contractible. -/
+theorem acute_cover_contractible_of_multiplicity_lt [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
+    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (V : ι → Set (sphere (0 : E) 1))
+    (hopen : ∀ i, IsOpen (V i)) (hcover : ∀ x, ∃ i, x ∈ V i)
+    (c : ι → sphere (0 : E) 1) (hc : ∀ i, c i ∈ V i)
+    (hacute : ∀ i, ∀ x ∈ V i, ∀ y ∈ V i, 0 < ⟪(x : E), (y : E)⟫_ℝ)
+    (hdim : 0 < finrank ℝ E)
+    (hcard : ∀ x, (Finset.univ.filter fun i => x ∈ V i).card < finrank ℝ E) :
+    ContractibleSpace (sphere (0 : E) 1) := by
+  obtain ⟨g, hid, hspan⟩ := acute_cover_normalized_map V hopen hcover c hc hacute
+  obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := map_omits_point_of_small_spans V (fun i => (c i : E)) g hdim hcard hspan

+/-- An open orthogonality-free cover whose point multiplicities are below the ambient

+theorem open_cover_contractible_of_multiplicity_lt {n k : ℕ} [Fact (finrank ℝ E = n + 1)]

+  letI : FiniteDimensional ℝ E :=

+  let V : t → Set (sphere (0 : E) 1) := fun j => j.val.2
+  choose c hc using fun j : t => (ht j.val j.property).2.1
+  have hVc : ∀ x, ∃ j, x ∈ V j := by
+    intro x
+    obtain ⟨j, hj, hx⟩ := htc x
+    exact ⟨⟨j, hj⟩, hx⟩
+  have hdim : finrank ℝ E = n + 1 := Fact.out
+  apply acute_cover_contractible_of_multiplicity_lt V

+    (fun j => (ht j.val j.property).2.2.2)

+    (hcover : ∀ x, ∃ i, x ∈ U i) (hfree : ∀ i, OrthogonalityFree (U i))

+  classical

+  intro x
+  have := cover_color_multiplicity (n := n) U hcover hfree x
+  omega

+theorem sphere_open_orthogonality_free_cover_lower_bound {n k : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n)

+    (hopen : ∀ i, IsOpen (U i)) (hcover : ∀ x, ∃ i, x ∈ U i)

+  letI : Fact (finrank ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) = (n - 1) + 1) :=
+    ⟨by simp only [finrank_euclideanSpace_fin]; omega⟩
+  apply SphereBrouwerObstruction.not_contractible_unit_sphere n (by omega)
+  apply low_color_cover_contractible (n := n - 1) U hopen hcover hfree
+  omega

+/-- Restriction to the perpendicular unit circle requires at least three absent colors. -/
+theorem sphere_three_absent_colors {k : ℕ}
+    (U : Fin k → Set (sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) 1))
+    (hopen : ∀ i, IsOpen (U i)) (hcover : ∀ x, ∃ i, x ∈ U i)
+    (hfree : ∀ i, OrthogonalityFree (U i))
+    (x : sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) 1) :
+    3 ≤ (Finset.univ.filter fun i => x ∉ U i).card := by
+  classical
+  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)
+  letI : Fact (finrank ℝ E = 2 + 1) := ⟨by simp [E]⟩
+  let b := OrthonormalBasis.fromOrthogonalSpanSingleton (𝕜 := ℝ) 2
+    (ne_zero_of_mem_unit_sphere x)
+  let f : sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) 1 → sphere (0 : E) 1 :=
+    fun y => ⟨(b.repr.symm y.val : E), by
+      rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm]
+      change ‖b.repr.symm y.val‖ = 1
+      rw [b.repr.symm.norm_map, mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.mp y.property]⟩
+  have hf : Continuous f := by
+    apply Continuous.subtype_mk
+    exact continuous_subtype_val.comp (b.repr.symm.continuous.comp continuous_subtype_val)
+  have hperp : ∀ y, ⟪(x : E), (f y : E)⟫_ℝ = 0 := by
+    intro y
+    exact Submodule.mem_orthogonal_singleton_iff_inner_right.mp (b.repr.symm y.val).property
+  let t := Finset.univ.filter fun i => x ∉ U i
+  let e : Fin (Fintype.card t) ≃ t := (Fintype.equivFin t).symm
+  let V : Fin (Fintype.card t) → Set (sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) 1) :=
+    fun j => f ⁻¹' U (e j).val
+  have hVcover : ∀ y, ∃ j, y ∈ V j := by
+    intro y
+    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := hcover (f y)
+    have hx : x ∉ U i := fun hxi => hfree i x hxi (f y) hi (hperp y)
+    let j : t := ⟨i, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, hx⟩⟩
+    refine ⟨e.symm j, ?_⟩
+    simpa [V, j] using hi
+  have hVfree : ∀ j, OrthogonalityFree (V j) := by

+  simpa only [Fintype.card_coe, Nat.reduceMul, Nat.reduceSub] using h

+least six members. The perpendicular circle supplies the strengthened point multiplicity. -/
+theorem sphere_two_open_orthogonality_free_cover_lower_six {k : ℕ}
+    (U : Fin k → Set (sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) 1))
+    (hopen : ∀ i, IsOpen (U i)) (hcover : ∀ x, ∃ i, x ∈ U i)
+    (hfree : ∀ i, OrthogonalityFree (U i)) : 6 ≤ k := by
+  classical
+  by_contra hk
+  letI : Fact (finrank ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) = 2 + 1) := ⟨by simp⟩
+  apply SphereBrouwerObstruction.not_contractible_unit_sphere 3 (by omega)
+  apply open_cover_contractible_of_multiplicity_lt (n := 2) U hopen hcover hfree
+  intro x
+  have habsent := sphere_three_absent_colors U hopen hcover hfree x
+  have hsum := Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not (s := Finset.univ)
+    (p := fun i => x ∈ U i)
+  simp only [Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin] at hsum
+  omega
+
+end D5.S3.Topology.SphereOrthogonalityCover

+# Alternating sums
+
+This file gives a telescoping formula for alternating sums of consecutive pairs in an additive
+commutative group, and the cancellation of alternating double sums whose terms satisfy the
+simplicial identity, which is the combinatorial core of `d ∘ d = 0` for alternating face map
+differentials. It also provides finite Euler sums for explicitly supported `ℤ`-graded families,
+including support independence, additivity, and translation of the grading.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+variable {G : Type*} [AddCommGroup G]
+
+/-! ### Finite Euler sums -/
+
+/-- The Euler sum of a `ℤ`-indexed family over an explicit finite set of degrees. -/
+def finiteEulerSum (f : ℤ → G) (s : Finset ℤ) : G :=
+  ∑ n ∈ s, (n.negOnePow : ℤ) • f n
+
+/-- A finite Euler sum is the alternating sum over its chosen finite set of degrees. -/
+theorem finiteEulerSum_def (f : ℤ → G) (s : Finset ℤ) :
+    finiteEulerSum f s = ∑ n ∈ s, (n.negOnePow : ℤ) • f n := by
+  rw [finiteEulerSum]
+
+@[simp]
+theorem finiteEulerSum_empty (f : ℤ → G) : finiteEulerSum f ∅ = 0 := by
+  simp [finiteEulerSum]
+
+@[simp]
+theorem finiteEulerSum_insert (f : ℤ → G) {s : Finset ℤ} {n : ℤ} (hn : n ∉ s) :
+    finiteEulerSum f (insert n s) = (n.negOnePow : ℤ) • f n + finiteEulerSum f s := by
+  simp [finiteEulerSum, hn]
+
+/-- Pointwise equal families have equal Euler sums over the same finite set. -/
+theorem finiteEulerSum_congr {f g : ℤ → G} {s : Finset ℤ} (h : ∀ n ∈ s, f n = g n) :
+    finiteEulerSum f s = finiteEulerSum g s := by
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro n hn
+  rw [h n hn]
+
+@[simp]
+theorem finiteEulerSum_zero (s : Finset ℤ) : finiteEulerSum (fun _ ↦ (0 : G)) s = 0 := by
+  simp [finiteEulerSum]
+
+/-- Euler sums distribute over pointwise addition. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem finiteEulerSum_add (f g : ℤ → G) (s : Finset ℤ) :
+    finiteEulerSum (fun n ↦ f n + g n) s = finiteEulerSum f s + finiteEulerSum g s := by
+  simp only [finiteEulerSum, smul_add, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
+
+/-- Two finite sets supporting the same family compute the same Euler sum. -/
+theorem finiteEulerSum_eq_of_eq_zero (f : ℤ → G) {s t : Finset ℤ}
+    (hs : ∀ n, n ∉ s → f n = 0) (ht : ∀ n, n ∉ t → f n = 0) :
+    finiteEulerSum f s = finiteEulerSum f t := by
+  have hsu : finiteEulerSum f s = finiteEulerSum f (s ∪ t) :=
+    Finset.sum_subset Finset.subset_union_left fun n _ hn ↦ by
+      rw [hs n hn, smul_zero]
+  have htu : finiteEulerSum f t = finiteEulerSum f (s ∪ t) :=
+    Finset.sum_subset Finset.subset_union_right fun n _ hn ↦ by
+      rw [ht n hn, smul_zero]
+  rw [hsu, htu]
+
+/-- Translating the grading by `m` multiplies its Euler sum by `(-1)ᵐ`. The set on the right is
+the corresponding translate of the finite summation range. -/
+theorem finiteEulerSum_reindex_add (f : ℤ → G) (m : ℤ) (s : Finset ℤ) :
+    finiteEulerSum (fun n ↦ f (n + m)) s =
+      (m.negOnePow : ℤ) •
+        finiteEulerSum f (s.map (Equiv.addRight m).toEmbedding) := by
+  rw [finiteEulerSum, finiteEulerSum, Finset.sum_map, Finset.smul_sum]
+  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun n _ ↦ ?_
+  simp only [Equiv.coe_toEmbedding, Equiv.coe_addRight, Int.negOnePow_add,
+    Units.val_mul, smul_smul]
+  rw [mul_left_comm, ← Units.val_mul, Int.units_mul_self]
+  simp
+
+/-! ### Telescoping and simplicial sums -/
+
+/-- An alternating sum of consecutive pairs telescopes to its two end terms. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem sum_Icc_negOnePow_smul_add (f : ℤ → G) (a b : ℤ)
+    (hab : a ≤ b) :
+    ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc a b, ((n.negOnePow : ℤ) • f n + (n.negOnePow : ℤ) • f (n + 1)) =
+      (a.negOnePow : ℤ) • f a + (b.negOnePow : ℤ) • f (b + 1) := by
+  induction b, hab using Int.leInduction with
+  | base => simp
+  | succ b hb ih =>
+    have hins : Finset.Icc a (b + 1) = insert (b + 1) (Finset.Icc a b) := by
+      ext x
+      simp only [Finset.mem_Icc, Finset.mem_insert]
+      omega
+    rw [hins, Finset.sum_insert (by simp), ih, Int.negOnePow_succ]
+    simp only [Units.val_neg, neg_smul]
+    abel
+
+/-- An alternating double sum `∑ i, (-1)ⁱ • ∑ j, (-1)ʲ • F i j` vanishes when its terms satisfy
+the simplicial identity `F (j + 1) i = F i j` for `i ≤ j`: the terms with `i ≤ j` cancel against
+those with `j < i`. With `F i j = φ (d_j (d_i x))` this is `d ∘ d = 0` for an alternating sum of
+faces `dᵢ`; the argument is that of Mathlib's
+`AlgebraicTopology.AlternatingFaceMapComplex.d_squared`. -/
+theorem sum_neg_one_pow_smul_sum_neg_one_pow_smul_eq_zero {G : Type*} [AddCommGroup G] {n : ℕ}
+    (F : Fin (n + 3) → Fin (n + 2) → G)
+    (hF : ∀ i j : Fin (n + 2), i ≤ j → F j.succ i = F i.castSucc j) :
+    ∑ i : Fin (n + 3), (-1 : ℤ) ^ (i : ℕ) • ∑ j : Fin (n + 2), (-1 : ℤ) ^ (j : ℕ) • F i j = 0 := by
+  simp only [Finset.smul_sum, smul_smul, ← pow_add, ← Finset.sum_product']
+  -- split the index set into the pairs with `i ≤ j` and their complement
+  let S : Finset (Fin (n + 3) × Fin (n + 2)) := {ij | (ij.1 : ℕ) ≤ ij.2}
+  rw [Finset.univ_product_univ, ← Finset.sum_add_sum_compl S, ← eq_neg_iff_add_eq_zero,
+    ← Finset.sum_neg_distrib]
+  -- the bijection `(i, j) ↦ (j + 1, i)` from `S` to its complement matches opposite terms
+  refine Finset.sum_bij (fun ij hij ↦ (ij.2.succ, ij.1.castLT
+      (lt_of_le_of_lt (Finset.mem_filter.1 hij).2 ij.2.is_lt))) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
+  · intro ij hij
+    simp only [S, Finset.compl_filter, Finset.mem_filter_univ, Fin.val_succ,
+      Fin.val_castLT] at hij ⊢
+    omega
+  · rintro ⟨i, j⟩ hij ⟨i', j'⟩ hij' h
+    simp only [Prod.mk.injEq, Fin.succ_inj] at h
+    ext
+    · simpa using congrArg Fin.val h.2
+    · exact congrArg Fin.val h.1
+  · rintro ⟨i', j'⟩ hij'
+    simp only [S, Finset.compl_filter, Finset.mem_filter_univ, not_le] at hij'
+    refine ⟨(Fin.castSucc j', i'.pred fun h ↦ by simp [h] at hij'), ?_, ?_⟩
+    · simp only [S, Finset.mem_filter_univ, Fin.val_castSucc, Fin.val_pred]
+      omega
+    · simp
+  · rintro ⟨i, j⟩ hij
+    have hij : (i : ℕ) ≤ j := (Finset.mem_filter.1 hij).2
+    dsimp only
+    rw [hF _ _ (by simpa [Fin.le_def] using hij), Fin.castSucc_castLT, Fin.val_succ,
+      Fin.val_castLT, ← neg_smul]
+    congr 1
+    ring
+
+end TauCeti

+/-!
+# Additional API for homological complexes
+
+This file records additivity of the cycles functor, degreewise recursion for powers of a
+complex endomorphism, and the existence of coproducts of complexes, computed degreewise. It also
+records the basic properties of the maps
+`K.toCycles i j : K.X i ⟶ K.cycles j` induced by the differentials: they kill the cycles in degree
+`i`, commute with morphisms of complexes, vanish after a morphism from a complex concentrated in
+degree `i`, and are epimorphisms in degrees where the complex is exact. In a degree with no nonzero
+differential into it, the identification of the homology with the cycles is natural
+(`HomologicalComplex.isoHomologyπ_inv_naturality`). The sequence
+`Zᵢ ⟶ Kᵢ ⟶ Zⱼ` of cycles is exact when `j = c.next i`
+(`HomologicalComplex.cyclesShortComplex_exact`). For adjacent degrees `i` and `j`, the cycles of a
+complex exact in degree `j` fit into a short exact sequence `0 ⟶ Zᵢ ⟶ Kᵢ ⟶ Zⱼ ⟶ 0`
+(`HomologicalComplex.cyclesShortComplex_shortExact`). Constructing the bundled cycle sequence
+requires homology only in the two selected degrees.
+The exactness results additionally require homology of the cycle sequence itself.
+For chain complexes indexed by the natural numbers, the identification of zero chains with
+cycles is natural (`ChainComplex.cycles₀Iso_inv_naturality`). The isomorphisms `homologyIsoSc'`
+are natural (`HomologicalComplex.homologyMap_comp_homologyIsoSc'_hom`).
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open CategoryTheory Limits
+
+universe w v u
+
+namespace HomologicalComplex
+
+variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasZeroMorphisms C] {ι : Type*}
+  {c : ComplexShape ι} {K : HomologicalComplex C c} {s : K ⟶ K}
+
+/-- Degreewise recursion for the powers of a chain endomorphism. -/
+lemma pow_f_succ (m : ℕ) (i : ι) :
+    (End.of s ^ (m + 1)).asHom.f i = (End.of s ^ m).asHom.f i ≫ s.f i := by
+  rw [pow_succ', End.mul_asHom, comp_f]
+
+/-- Homological complexes have the coproducts that the underlying category has. They are
+computed degreewise. -/
+instance hasCoproducts [HasCoproducts.{w} C] : HasCoproducts.{w} (HomologicalComplex C c) :=
+  fun _ ↦ inferInstance
+
+/-! ### The maps onto the cycles -/
+
+section Cycles
+
+variable (K) {L : HomologicalComplex C c}
+
+/-- The map from the cycles in degree `i` to the cycles in degree `j` induced by the differential
+vanishes. -/
+@[reassoc]
+lemma iCycles_toCycles (i j : ι) [K.HasHomology i] [K.HasHomology j] :
+    K.iCycles i ≫ K.toCycles i j = 0 := by
+  rw [← cancel_mono (K.iCycles j), Category.assoc, toCycles_i, iCycles_d, zero_comp]
+
+/-- The short complex `Zᵢ(K) ⟶ Kᵢ ⟶ Zⱼ(K)` cut out of a homological complex. Its
+second map is the differential with codomain restricted to the cycles in degree `j`. -/
+noncomputable def cyclesShortComplex (i j : ι) [K.HasHomology i] [K.HasHomology j] :
+    ShortComplex C :=
+  ShortComplex.mk (K.iCycles i) (K.toCycles i j) (K.iCycles_toCycles i j)
+
+/-- The cycle sequence is formed by the inclusion of cycles and the corestricted differential. -/
+lemma cyclesShortComplex_def (i j : ι) [K.HasHomology i] [K.HasHomology j] :
+    K.cyclesShortComplex i j =
+      ShortComplex.mk (K.iCycles i) (K.toCycles i j) (K.iCycles_toCycles i j) := (rfl)
+
+@[simp]
+lemma cyclesShortComplex_X₁ (i j : ι) [K.HasHomology i] [K.HasHomology j] :
+    (K.cyclesShortComplex i j).X₁ = K.cycles i := (rfl)
+
+@[simp]
+lemma cyclesShortComplex_X₂ (i j : ι) [K.HasHomology i] [K.HasHomology j] :
+    (K.cyclesShortComplex i j).X₂ = K.X i := (rfl)
+
+@[simp]
+lemma cyclesShortComplex_X₃ (i j : ι) [K.HasHomology i] [K.HasHomology j] :
+    (K.cyclesShortComplex i j).X₃ = K.cycles j := (rfl)
+
+/-- The first map of the cycle sequence is the inclusion of cycles, transported along the
+object equalities `cyclesShortComplex_X₁` and `cyclesShortComplex_X₂`. -/
+@[simp]
+lemma cyclesShortComplex_f (i j : ι) [K.HasHomology i] [K.HasHomology j] :
+    (K.cyclesShortComplex i j).f = eqToHom (K.cyclesShortComplex_X₁ i j) ≫ K.iCycles i ≫
+      eqToHom (K.cyclesShortComplex_X₂ i j).symm :=
+  (Category.comp_id _).symm.trans (Category.id_comp _).symm
+
+/-- The second map of the cycle sequence is the corestricted differential, transported along the
+object equalities `cyclesShortComplex_X₂` and `cyclesShortComplex_X₃`. -/
+@[simp]
+lemma cyclesShortComplex_g (i j : ι) [K.HasHomology i] [K.HasHomology j] :
+    (K.cyclesShortComplex i j).g = eqToHom (K.cyclesShortComplex_X₂ i j) ≫ K.toCycles i j ≫
+      eqToHom (K.cyclesShortComplex_X₃ i j).symm :=
+  (Category.comp_id _).symm.trans (Category.id_comp _).symm
+
+variable {K}
+
+/-- The maps onto the cycles induced by the differentials commute with morphisms of complexes. -/
+@[reassoc]
+lemma toCycles_cyclesMap (φ : K ⟶ L) (i j : ι) [K.HasHomology j] [L.HasHomology j] :
+    K.toCycles i j ≫ cyclesMap φ j = φ.f i ≫ L.toCycles i j :=
+  (cancel_mono (L.iCycles j)).1 <| by simp
+
+/-- In a degree `j` with no nonzero differential into it, the identifications
+`K.isoHomologyπ i j` of the homology with the cycles commute with the maps induced by a morphism of
+complexes. -/
+@[reassoc]
+lemma isoHomologyπ_inv_naturality (φ : K ⟶ L) (i j : ι) (hi : c.prev j = i) (hK : K.d i j = 0)
+    (hL : L.d i j = 0) [K.HasHomology j] [L.HasHomology j] :
+    homologyMap φ j ≫ (L.isoHomologyπ i j hi hL).inv =
+      (K.isoHomologyπ i j hi hK).inv ≫ cyclesMap φ j := by
+  rw [← cancel_epi (K.isoHomologyπ i j hi hK).hom]
+  simp
+
+variable [HasZeroObject C] [DecidableEq ι] {i : ι} {X : C}
+
+/-- A morphism from a complex concentrated in degree `i` vanishes after the differential out of
+degree `i`. -/
+@[reassoc]
+lemma single_f_d (g : (single C c i).obj X ⟶ L) (j : ι) : g.f i ≫ L.d i j = 0 := by
+  rw [g.comm i j, single_obj_d, zero_comp]
+
+/-- A morphism from a complex concentrated in degree `i` vanishes after the map onto the cycles in
+degree `j`. -/
+@[reassoc]
+lemma single_f_toCycles (g : (single C c i).obj X ⟶ L) (j : ι) [L.HasHomology j] :
+    g.f i ≫ L.toCycles i j = 0 := by
+  rw [← cancel_mono (L.iCycles j), Category.assoc, toCycles_i, single_f_d, zero_comp]
+
+end Cycles
+
+end HomologicalComplex
+
+namespace HomologicalComplex
+
+variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasZeroMorphisms C] {ι : Type*}
+  {c : ComplexShape ι} {K : HomologicalComplex C c}
+
+variable (K) in
+/-- The sequence `Zᵢ ⟶ Kᵢ ⟶ Zⱼ` of the cycles of a complex `K` is exact when `j` is the degree
+following `i`: the cycles in degree `i` are the kernel of the differential. -/
+lemma cyclesShortComplex_exact (i j : ι) [K.HasHomology i] [K.HasHomology j]
+    [hH : (K.cyclesShortComplex i j).HasHomology] (hij : c.next i = j) :
+    (K.cyclesShortComplex i j).Exact := by
+  rw [cyclesShortComplex_def] at hH ⊢
+  let S := ShortComplex.mk _ _ (K.iCycles_toCycles i j)
+  have hS := isKernelOfComp (K.iCycles j) (K.d i j) (K.cyclesIsKernel i j hij)
+    (K.iCycles_toCycles i j) (K.toCycles_i i j)
+  rw [S.exact_iff_iCycles_pOpcycles_zero]
+  have h : hS.lift (KernelFork.ofι S.iCycles S.iCycles_g) ≫ S.f = S.iCycles :=
+    Fork.IsLimit.lift_ι _
+  rw [← h, Category.assoc, S.f_pOpcycles, comp_zero]
+
+end HomologicalComplex
+
+namespace HomologicalComplex
+
+variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Preadditive C] {ι : Type*}
+  {c : ComplexShape ι} {K : HomologicalComplex C c}
+
+/-- In a complex exact in degree `j`, the map onto the cycles in degree `j` from the preceding
+degree is an epimorphism. -/
+lemma epi_toCycles_of_exactAt {i j : ι} [K.HasHomology j]
+    (h : K.ExactAt j) (hij : c.prev j = i) :
+    Epi (K.toCycles i j) := by
+  rw [exactAt_iff' _ i j (c.next j) hij rfl] at h
+  have := h.hasHomology
+  rw [← epi_comp_iff_of_isIso _ (K.cyclesIsoSc' i j (c.next j) hij rfl).hom,
+    K.toCycles_cyclesIsoSc'_hom]
+  exact h.epi_toCycles
+
+/-- The cycle sequence `Zᵢ(K) ⟶ Kᵢ ⟶ Zⱼ(K)` is short exact when `i` and `j` are adjacent
+and `K` is exact in degree `j`. -/
+lemma cyclesShortComplex_shortExact (i j : ι) [K.HasHomology i] [K.HasHomology j]
+    [(K.cyclesShortComplex i j).HasHomology]
+    (hij : c.Rel i j) (hK : K.ExactAt j) : (K.cyclesShortComplex i j).ShortExact := by
+  have hE := K.cyclesShortComplex_exact i j (c.next_eq' hij)
+  rw [cyclesShortComplex_def] at hE ⊢
+  exact ShortComplex.ShortExact.mk' hE
+    inferInstance (epi_toCycles_of_exactAt hK (c.prev_eq' hij))
+
+end HomologicalComplex
+
+namespace HomologicalComplex
+
+variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Preadditive C] {ι : Type*} {c : ComplexShape ι}
+  {K L : HomologicalComplex C c}
+
+/-- Taking cycles is additive on morphisms of complexes. -/
+@[simp]
+lemma cyclesMap_add (f g : K ⟶ L) (i : ι) [K.HasHomology i] [L.HasHomology i] :
+    cyclesMap (f + g) i = cyclesMap f i + cyclesMap g i := by
+  apply (cancel_mono (L.iCycles i)).1
+  simp only [Preadditive.add_comp, cyclesMap_i, add_f_apply, Preadditive.comp_add]
+
+instance cyclesFunctor_additive [CategoryWithHomology C] (i : ι) :
+    (cyclesFunctor C c i).Additive where
+  map_add := by
+    intro X Y f g
+    -- `cyclesFunctor` is opaque, so expose its defining map before applying the map-level API.
+    change cyclesMap (f + g) i = cyclesMap f i + cyclesMap g i
+    exact cyclesMap_add f g i
+
+section HomologyIsoSc'
+
+variable {C : Type*} [Category* C] [HasZeroMorphisms C] {ι : Type*}
+  {c : ComplexShape ι} {K L : HomologicalComplex C c} (f : K ⟶ L) (i j k : ι)
+  (hi : c.prev j = i) (hk : c.next j = k) [K.HasHomology j] [L.HasHomology j]
+  [(K.sc' i j k).HasHomology] [(L.sc' i j k).HasHomology]
+
+/-- The isomorphisms `homologyIsoSc'` are natural (this is the naturality of Mathlib's
+`homologyFunctorIso'`, for complexes which only individually have homology). -/
+@[reassoc]
+lemma homologyMap_comp_homologyIsoSc'_hom :
+    homologyMap f j ≫ (L.homologyIsoSc' i j k hi hk).hom =
+      (K.homologyIsoSc' i j k hi hk).hom ≫
+        ShortComplex.homologyMap ((shortComplexFunctor' C c i j k).map f) := by
+  rw [homologyIsoSc', homologyIsoSc', ShortComplex.homologyMapIso_hom,
+    ShortComplex.homologyMapIso_hom, homologyMap]
+  -- the source of `homologyMap f j` is `K.homology j`, which is `(K.sc j).homology` only up to
+  -- unfolding `HomologicalComplex.homology`, so the generic `homologyMap_comp` needs `erw`
+  erw [← ShortComplex.homologyMap_comp, ← ShortComplex.homologyMap_comp]
+  congr 1
+  exact (natIsoSc' C c i j k hi hk).hom.naturality f
+
+end HomologyIsoSc'
+
+end HomologicalComplex
+
+namespace ChainComplex
+
+variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasZeroMorphisms C]
+  {K L : ChainComplex C ℕ} [K.HasHomology 0] [L.HasHomology 0]
+
+/-- The identification of degree-zero chains with degree-zero cycles is natural. -/
+@[reassoc]
+lemma cycles₀Iso_inv_naturality (φ : K ⟶ L) :
+    K.cycles₀Iso.inv ≫ HomologicalComplex.cyclesMap φ 0 =
+      φ.f 0 ≫ L.cycles₀Iso.inv := by
+  apply (cancel_mono (L.iCycles 0)).1
+  simp
+
+end ChainComplex
+
+namespace HomologicalComplex
+
+section HomologyTransport
+
+variable {C : Type*} [Category* C] [HasZeroMorphisms C] [CategoryWithHomology C]
+  {ι : Type*} {c : ComplexShape ι} {L L' M M' : HomologicalComplex C c}
+
+/-- A morphism transported along equalities of complexes induces the corresponding transport
+of the homology map. -/
+lemma homologyMap_comp_eqToHom (ψ : L ⟶ L') (hM : M = L) (hM' : M' = L')
+    (τ : M ⟶ M') (hτ : τ = eqToHom hM ≫ ψ ≫ eqToHom hM'.symm) (q : ι) :
+    homologyMap τ q ≫ eqToHom (congrArg (·.homology q) hM') =
+      eqToHom (congrArg (·.homology q) hM) ≫ homologyMap ψ q := by
+  subst hM hM' hτ
+  simp
+
+end HomologyTransport
+
+end HomologicalComplex

+# The homology sequence of a short exact sequence with a biproduct middle term
+
+Let `X ⟶ A ⊞ B ⟶ Z` be a short exact sequence of homological complexes in an abelian category,
+with first map `(f₁, f₂)` and second map `g₁ + g₂`. Since homology commutes with binary
+biproducts, its homology long exact sequence can be written through `H(A) ⊞ H(B)`:
+`⋯ ⟶ Hᵢ(X) ⟶ Hᵢ(A) ⊞ Hᵢ(B) ⟶ Hᵢ(Z) ⟶ Hⱼ(X) ⟶ ⋯`, with first map `(f₁_*, f₂_*)`, second map
+`g₁_* + g₂_*` and the connecting morphism of the short exact sequence. This is the form of the
+Mayer–Vietoris sequences, both in homology and in cohomology.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact.biprod_homology_exact₁`,
+  `CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact.biprod_homology_exact₂`,
+  `CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact.biprod_homology_exact₃`: exactness of this sequence at
+  `Hⱼ(X)`, at `Hᵢ(A) ⊞ Hᵢ(B)` and at `Hᵢ(Z)`.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open CategoryTheory Limits
+
+attribute [local instance] preservesBinaryBiproduct_of_preservesBiproduct
+
+namespace HomologicalComplex
+
+variable {C ι : Type*} [Category* C] [Abelian C] {c : ComplexShape ι}
+  {X A B Z : HomologicalComplex C c} {f₁ : X ⟶ A} {f₂ : X ⟶ B} {g₁ : A ⟶ Z} {g₂ : B ⟶ Z}
+
+/-- The maps induced on homology by the components of `X ⟶ A ⊞ B ⟶ Z` compose to zero. -/
+@[reassoc]
+lemma biprod_lift_homologyMap_comp_desc_homologyMap
+    (w : biprod.lift f₁ f₂ ≫ biprod.desc g₁ g₂ = 0) (i : ι) :
+    biprod.lift (homologyMap f₁ i) (homologyMap f₂ i) ≫
+      biprod.desc (homologyMap g₁ i) (homologyMap g₂ i) = 0 := by
+  rw [biprod.lift_desc, ← homologyMap_comp, ← homologyMap_comp, ← homologyMap_add,
+    ← biprod.lift_desc, w, homologyMap_zero]
+
+variable (A B) in
+/-- Homology commutes with the binary biproduct `A ⊞ B`. -/
+private noncomputable abbrev homologyBiprodIso (i : ι) :
+    (A ⊞ B).homology i ≅ A.homology i ⊞ B.homology i :=
+  (homologyFunctor C c i).mapBiprod A B
+
+private lemma homologyMap_lift_comp_homologyBiprodIso_hom (i : ι) :
+    homologyMap (biprod.lift f₁ f₂) i ≫ (homologyBiprodIso A B i).hom =
+      biprod.lift (homologyMap f₁ i) (homologyMap f₂ i) :=
+  biprod.map_lift_mapBiprod (homologyFunctor C c i) _ _ _ _
+
+@[reassoc]
+private lemma homologyBiprodIso_hom_comp_desc_homologyMap (i : ι) :
+    (homologyBiprodIso A B i).hom ≫
+        biprod.desc (homologyMap g₁ i) (homologyMap g₂ i) =
+      homologyMap (biprod.desc g₁ g₂) i :=
+  biprod.mapBiprod_hom_desc (homologyFunctor C c i) _ _ _ _
+
+/-- The map `Hᵢ(X) ⟶ Hᵢ(A) ⊞ Hᵢ(B)` induced by `(f₁, f₂)` is a monomorphism when the map induced
+by `biprod.lift f₁ f₂` is. -/
+lemma mono_biprod_lift_homologyMap (i : ι) [Mono (homologyMap (biprod.lift f₁ f₂) i)] :
+    Mono (biprod.lift (homologyMap f₁ i) (homologyMap f₂ i)) := by
+  rw [← homologyMap_lift_comp_homologyBiprodIso_hom]
+  infer_instance
+
+/-- The map `Hᵢ(A) ⊞ Hᵢ(B) ⟶ Hᵢ(Z)` induced by `g₁ + g₂` is an epimorphism when the map induced
+by `biprod.desc g₁ g₂` is. -/
+lemma epi_biprod_desc_homologyMap (i : ι) [Epi (homologyMap (biprod.desc g₁ g₂) i)] :
+    Epi (biprod.desc (homologyMap g₁ i) (homologyMap g₂ i)) :=
+  (epi_comp_iff_of_epi (homologyBiprodIso A B i).hom _).1
+    (by rw [homologyBiprodIso_hom_comp_desc_homologyMap]; infer_instance)
+
+end HomologicalComplex
+
+namespace CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact
+
+open HomologicalComplex
+
+variable {C ι : Type*} [Category* C] [Abelian C] {c : ComplexShape ι}
+  {X A B Z : HomologicalComplex C c} {f₁ : X ⟶ A} {f₂ : X ⟶ B} {g₁ : A ⟶ Z} {g₂ : B ⟶ Z}
+  {w : biprod.lift f₁ f₂ ≫ biprod.desc g₁ g₂ = 0} (hS : (ShortComplex.mk _ _ w).ShortExact)
+
+include hS
+
+/-- The connecting morphism of a short exact sequence `X ⟶ A ⊞ B ⟶ Z` followed by the map
+`Hⱼ(X) ⟶ Hⱼ(A) ⊞ Hⱼ(B)` is zero. -/
+@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
+lemma δ_comp_biprod_lift_homologyMap (i j : ι) (hij : c.Rel i j) :
+    hS.δ i j hij ≫
+      biprod.lift (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap f₁ j) (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap f₂ j) =
+        0 := by
+  rw [← homologyMap_lift_comp_homologyBiprodIso_hom]
+  exact hS.δ_comp_assoc i j hij _ |>.trans zero_comp
+
+/-- The map `Hᵢ(A) ⊞ Hᵢ(B) ⟶ Hᵢ(Z)` induced by a short exact sequence `X ⟶ A ⊞ B ⟶ Z` followed
+by its connecting morphism is zero. -/
+@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
+lemma biprod_desc_homologyMap_comp_δ (i j : ι) (hij : c.Rel i j) :
+    biprod.desc (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap g₁ i) (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap g₂ i) ≫
+      hS.δ i j hij = 0 := by
+  rw [← cancel_epi (homologyBiprodIso A B i).hom, comp_zero,
+    homologyBiprodIso_hom_comp_desc_homologyMap_assoc]
+  exact hS.comp_δ i j hij
+
+/-- Exactness at `Hⱼ(X)` of the homology sequence of a short exact sequence `X ⟶ A ⊞ B ⟶ Z`. -/
+lemma biprod_homology_exact₁ (i j : ι) (hij : c.Rel i j) :
+    (ShortComplex.mk _ _ (hS.δ_comp_biprod_lift_homologyMap i j hij)).Exact := by
+  refine (ShortComplex.exact_iff_of_iso ?_).1 (hS.homology_exact₁ i j hij)
+  refine ShortComplex.isoMk (Iso.refl _) (Iso.refl _)
+    (homologyBiprodIso A B j) ?_ ?_
+  · simp
+  · exact (Category.id_comp _).trans (homologyMap_lift_comp_homologyBiprodIso_hom j).symm
+
+/-- Exactness at `Hᵢ(A) ⊞ Hᵢ(B)` of the homology sequence of a short exact sequence
+`X ⟶ A ⊞ B ⟶ Z`. -/
+lemma biprod_homology_exact₂ (i : ι) :
+    (ShortComplex.mk _ _
+      (HomologicalComplex.biprod_lift_homologyMap_comp_desc_homologyMap w i)).Exact := by
+  refine (ShortComplex.exact_iff_of_iso ?_).1 (hS.homology_exact₂ i)
+  refine ShortComplex.isoMk (Iso.refl _)
+    (homologyBiprodIso A B i) (Iso.refl _) ?_ ?_
+  · exact (Category.id_comp _).trans (homologyMap_lift_comp_homologyBiprodIso_hom i).symm
+  · exact (homologyBiprodIso_hom_comp_desc_homologyMap i).trans (Category.comp_id _).symm
+
+/-- Exactness at `Hᵢ(Z)` of the homology sequence of a short exact sequence `X ⟶ A ⊞ B ⟶ Z`. -/
+lemma biprod_homology_exact₃ (i j : ι) (hij : c.Rel i j) :
+    (ShortComplex.mk _ _ (hS.biprod_desc_homologyMap_comp_δ i j hij)).Exact := by
+  refine (ShortComplex.exact_iff_of_iso ?_).1 (hS.homology_exact₃ i j hij)
+  refine ShortComplex.isoMk (homologyBiprodIso A B i)
+    (Iso.refl _) (Iso.refl _) ?_ ?_
+  · exact (homologyBiprodIso_hom_comp_desc_homologyMap i).trans (Category.comp_id _).symm
+  · simp
+
+end CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact

+# Constructions on chain homotopies
+
+Three constructions of chain homotopies: two produce new homotopies from old ones, and the
+third assembles a null-homotopy from components given all at once.
+
+`Homotopy.descCokernel` descends a homotopy along a degreewise cokernel.  Let `p : L ⟶ M` exhibit
+`M` in each degree as the cokernel of `u : K ⟶ L`, and let `p' : L' ⟶ M'` be any morphism of
+complexes.  A chain homotopy between morphisms `L ⟶ L'` whose components send the image of `u`
+into the kernel of `p'` then descends to a chain homotopy between the induced morphisms `M ⟶ M'`.
+Only the source side is assumed to be a degreewise cokernel; on the target side the hypothesis is
+the bare vanishing `u.f i ≫ HL.hom i j ≫ p'.f j = 0`, which is what the universal property needs.
+This is the mechanism behind homotopy invariance of relative homology, where `M` is the relative
+chain complex of a pair, that is, the degreewise cokernel of the chains of the subspace, and the
+vanishing holds because the homotopy restricts to the subspace.
+
+`Homotopy.idPow` iterates a chain homotopy from the identity of `K` to an endomorphism `s`: it
+exhibits every power `sᵐ` as homotopic to the identity, through the explicit operator
+`∑_{k < m} sᵏ ≫ h`.  Its components are needed, and not just the existence of some homotopy, when
+`m` is allowed to vary from one summand of `K` to another, as in the proof that small singular
+chains for an open cover include as a chain homotopy equivalence.
+
+`Homotopy.mkChainComplex` builds a null-homotopy of a chain map between `ℕ`-indexed chain
+complexes from its components `h n : P.X n ⟶ Q.X (n + 1)`, given all at once together with the
+homotopy identities in degree zero and in positive degrees.  It is the non-inductive counterpart of
+Mathlib's `Homotopy.mkInductive`, for the situation where the components are constructed by a
+recursion of their own rather than one degree at a time from the previous two.
+
+`Homotopy.cyclesMap_sub_eq` expresses the difference of the maps on cycles induced by
+homotopic maps as a factorization through a term of the target complex. In particular, these
+maps agree after passing to a stable category that kills that term.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+noncomputable section
+
+open CategoryTheory Limits
+
+universe v u
+
+namespace Homotopy
+
+/-- On cycles, the difference of homotopic maps factors through the preceding target term.
+This identity does not require exactness of either complex. -/
+theorem cyclesMap_sub_eq {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Preadditive C]
+    {ι : Type*} {c : ComplexShape ι} {K L : HomologicalComplex C c} {f g : K ⟶ L}
+    (h : Homotopy f g) (i : ι) [K.HasHomology i] [L.HasHomology i] :
+    HomologicalComplex.cyclesMap f i - HomologicalComplex.cyclesMap g i =
+      K.iCycles i ≫ h.hom i (c.prev i) ≫ L.toCycles (c.prev i) i := by
+  apply (cancel_mono (L.iCycles i)).mp
+  simp only [Preadditive.sub_comp, HomologicalComplex.cyclesMap_i, Category.assoc,
+    HomologicalComplex.toCycles_i]
+  rw [h.comm i]
+  simp [dNext, prevD, Preadditive.comp_add, ← Category.assoc]
+
+variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Preadditive C] {ι : Type*} {c : ComplexShape ι}
+  {K L M L' M' : HomologicalComplex C c}
+  {fL gL : L ⟶ L'} {fM gM : M ⟶ M'}
+  (HL : Homotopy fL gL)
+  (u : K ⟶ L) (p : L ⟶ M) (p' : L' ⟶ M')
+  (hw : ∀ i, u.f i ≫ p.f i = 0)
+  (hp : ∀ i, IsColimit (CokernelCofork.ofπ (p.f i) (hw i)))
+  (hcomm : ∀ i j, u.f i ≫ HL.hom i j ≫ p'.f j = 0)
+
+include hw hp hcomm
+
+/-- The components of the chain homotopy that `Homotopy.descCokernel` obtains on the quotient
+complex `M`. -/
+@[no_expose]
+def descCokernelHom (i j : ι) : M.X i ⟶ M'.X j :=
+  (CokernelCofork.IsColimit.desc' (hp i) (HL.hom i j ≫ p'.f j) (hcomm i j)).1
+
+@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
+lemma π_descCokernelHom (i j : ι) :
+    p.f i ≫ descCokernelHom HL u p p' hw hp hcomm i j = HL.hom i j ≫ p'.f j :=
+  (CokernelCofork.IsColimit.desc' (hp i) (HL.hom i j ≫ p'.f j) (hcomm i j)).2
+
+private lemma π_comp_dNext (i : ι) :
+    p.f i ≫ dNext i (descCokernelHom HL u p p' hw hp hcomm) = dNext i HL.hom ≫ p'.f i := by
+  rw [← dNext_comp_left, ← dNext_comp_right]
+  exact congrArg (fun F ↦ dNext i F) (by funext a b; exact π_descCokernelHom ..)
+
+private lemma π_comp_prevD (i : ι) :
+    p.f i ≫ prevD i (descCokernelHom HL u p p' hw hp hcomm) = prevD i HL.hom ≫ p'.f i := by
+  rw [← prevD_comp_left, ← prevD_comp_right]
+  exact congrArg (fun F ↦ prevD i F) (by funext a b; exact π_descCokernelHom ..)
+
+/-- A chain homotopy on the total complexes whose components kill the subcomplex after composing
+with `p'` descends to a chain homotopy on the quotient complex `M`. -/
+@[no_expose]
+def descCokernel (hf : p ≫ fM = fL ≫ p') (hg : p ≫ gM = gL ≫ p') : Homotopy fM gM where
+  hom := descCokernelHom HL u p p' hw hp hcomm
+  zero i j hij := Cofork.IsColimit.hom_ext (hp i) (by simp [HL.zero i j hij])
+  comm i := Cofork.IsColimit.hom_ext (hp i) (by
+    simp only [Cofork.π_ofπ, Preadditive.comp_add, π_comp_dNext, π_comp_prevD,
+      ← HomologicalComplex.comp_f p fM, ← HomologicalComplex.comp_f p gM, hf, hg,
+      HomologicalComplex.comp_f]
+    rw [← Preadditive.add_comp, ← Preadditive.add_comp, ← HL.comm i])
+
+@[simp]
+lemma descCokernel_hom (hf : p ≫ fM = fL ≫ p') (hg : p ≫ gM = gL ≫ p') :
+    (descCokernel HL u p p' hw hp hcomm hf hg).hom = descCokernelHom HL u p p' hw hp hcomm := (rfl)
+
+@[reassoc]
+lemma π_descCokernel_hom (hf : p ≫ fM = fL ≫ p') (hg : p ≫ gM = gL ≫ p') (i j : ι) :
+    p.f i ≫ (descCokernel HL u p p' hw hp hcomm hf hg).hom i j = HL.hom i j ≫ p'.f j :=
+  π_descCokernelHom HL u p p' hw hp hcomm i j
+
+end Homotopy
+
+section Pow
+
+variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {ι : Type*} {c : ComplexShape ι}
+
+namespace Homotopy
+
+variable [Preadditive C] {K : HomologicalComplex C c} {s : K ⟶ K}
+
+/-- Iterating a chain homotopy from the identity.  If `h` is a chain homotopy from the identity of
+`K` to a chain endomorphism `s`, then `h.idPow m` is a chain homotopy from the identity to the
+`m`-th power of `s`, whose operator in bidegree `(i, j)` is `∑_{k < m} (sᵏ)ᵢ ≫ hᵢⱼ`. -/
+@[no_expose]
+def idPow (h : Homotopy (𝟙 K) s) (m : ℕ) : Homotopy (𝟙 K) (End.of s ^ m).asHom where
+  hom i j := ∑ k ∈ Finset.range m, (End.of s ^ k).asHom.f i ≫ h.hom i j
+  zero i j hij := by simp [h.zero i j hij]
+  comm i := by
+    have hdn : dNext i (fun a b ↦ ∑ k ∈ Finset.range m, (End.of s ^ k).asHom.f a ≫ h.hom a b) =
+        ∑ k ∈ Finset.range m, (End.of s ^ k).asHom.f i ≫ dNext i h.hom := by
+      simpa only [Finset.sum_fn, dNext_comp_left] using
+        map_sum (dNext i) (fun k a b ↦ (End.of s ^ k).asHom.f a ≫ h.hom a b) (Finset.range m)
+    have hpv : prevD i (fun a b ↦ ∑ k ∈ Finset.range m, (End.of s ^ k).asHom.f a ≫ h.hom a b) =
+        ∑ k ∈ Finset.range m, (End.of s ^ k).asHom.f i ≫ prevD i h.hom := by
+      simpa only [Finset.sum_fn, prevD_comp_left] using
+        map_sum (prevD i) (fun k a b ↦ (End.of s ^ k).asHom.f a ≫ h.hom a b) (Finset.range m)
+    have hstep : ∀ k ∈ Finset.range m, (End.of s ^ k).asHom.f i ≫ dNext i h.hom +
+        (End.of s ^ k).asHom.f i ≫ prevD i h.hom =
+        (End.of s ^ k).asHom.f i - (End.of s ^ (k + 1)).asHom.f i := fun k _ ↦ by
+      have hsum : dNext i h.hom + prevD i h.hom = 𝟙 (K.X i) - s.f i := by
+        have hc := h.comm i
+        rw [HomologicalComplex.id_f] at hc
+        rw [hc]
+        abel
+      rw [← Preadditive.comp_add, hsum, Preadditive.comp_sub, Category.comp_id,
+        HomologicalComplex.pow_f_succ]
+    rw [hdn, hpv, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_congr rfl hstep,
+      Finset.sum_range_sub' (fun k ↦ (End.of s ^ k).asHom.f i) m, pow_zero, End.one_asHom,
+      HomologicalComplex.id_f]
+    abel
+
+@[simp]
+lemma idPow_hom (h : Homotopy (𝟙 K) s) (m : ℕ) (i j : ι) :
+    (h.idPow m).hom i j = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range m, (End.of s ^ k).asHom.f i ≫ h.hom i j := (rfl)
+
+end Homotopy
+
+end Pow
+
+section MkChainComplex
+
+variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Preadditive C] {P Q : ChainComplex C ℕ}
+
+namespace Homotopy
+
+/-- A null-homotopy of a chain map `e : P ⟶ Q` between `ℕ`-indexed chain complexes, from its
+components `h n : P.X n ⟶ Q.X (n + 1)` and the homotopy identities `e.f 0 = h 0 ≫ d` and
+`e.f (n + 1) = d ≫ h n + h (n + 1) ≫ d`. The components are given all at once; compare
+`Homotopy.mkInductive`, which constructs them one degree at a time. -/
+@[no_expose]
+def mkChainComplex (e : P ⟶ Q) (h : ∀ n, P.X n ⟶ Q.X (n + 1)) (comm_zero : e.f 0 = h 0 ≫ Q.d 1 0)
+    (comm_succ : ∀ n, e.f (n + 1) = P.d (n + 1) n ≫ h n + h (n + 1) ≫ Q.d (n + 2) (n + 1)) :
+    Homotopy e 0 where
+  hom i j := if hij : i + 1 = j then h i ≫ eqToHom (congrArg Q.X hij) else 0
+  zero i j hij := dite_eq_right (by simpa [ComplexShape.down_Rel] using hij)
+  comm i := by
+    cases i with
+    | zero =>
+        rw [dNext_zero_chainComplex, prevD_chainComplex]
+        simpa using comm_zero
+    | succ i =>
+        rw [dNext_succ_chainComplex, prevD_chainComplex]
+        simpa using comm_succ i
+
+@[simp]
+lemma mkChainComplex_hom_succ (e : P ⟶ Q) (h : ∀ n, P.X n ⟶ Q.X (n + 1))
+    (comm_zero : e.f 0 = h 0 ≫ Q.d 1 0)
+    (comm_succ : ∀ n, e.f (n + 1) = P.d (n + 1) n ≫ h n + h (n + 1) ≫ Q.d (n + 2) (n + 1))
+    (n : ℕ) : (mkChainComplex e h comm_zero comm_succ).hom n (n + 1) = h n := by
+  simp [mkChainComplex]
+
+end Homotopy
+
+end MkChainComplex

+# The simplicial chain complex preserves colimits
+
+In degree `n` the chain complex of a simplicial set `X` with coefficients in an object `R` is the
+coproduct of copies of `R` indexed by the `n`-simplices of `X`.  Evaluating a simplicial set in a
+fixed degree preserves colimits, because colimits of presheaves are computed pointwise, and
+forming a coproduct of copies of `R` preserves colimits; hence so does `X ↦ X.chainComplex R`.
+
+The case of a coproduct is chain-level additivity: the chain complex of a disjoint union of
+simplicial sets is the coproduct of the chain complexes of the summands.
+The chain map induced by a monomorphism of simplicial sets is also a monomorphism.
+
+## Sources
+
+The argument assembles three Mathlib constructions.  The simplicial chain complex
+`SSet.chainComplexFunctor` and its degreewise cofan `SSet.isColimitChainComplexXCofan`
+are due to Joël Riou and Andrew Yang in `Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/SimplicialSet/Homology/Basic`;
+the coproduct-of-copies functor `CategoryTheory.Limits.sigmaConst` and its colimit preservation
+are due to Joël Riou in `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Preserves/SigmaConst`, as is the reduction
+of colimit preservation to the degreewise statement,
+`HomologicalComplex.preservesColimitsOfShape_of_eval`.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+noncomputable section
+
+open CategoryTheory Limits
+
+open scoped Simplicial
+
+universe w v u v' u'
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+variable (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] [HasCoproducts.{w} C] [Preadditive C] (R : C)
+
+variable {J : Type u'} [Category.{v'} J] [HasColimitsOfShape J (Type w)]
+
+/-- The simplicial chain complex with coefficients in `R` preserves every shape of colimit that
+the category of `w`-small types has: in each degree it is the composite of evaluation, which
+preserves colimits of presheaves, with `sigmaConst.obj R`. -/
+instance : PreservesColimitsOfShape J ((SSet.chainComplexFunctor.{w} C).obj R) :=
+  HomologicalComplex.preservesColimitsOfShape_of_eval _ fun n ↦ by
+    have : PreservesColimitsOfShape J
+        ((evaluation SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ (Type w)).obj (Opposite.op ⦋n⦌) ⋙ sigmaConst.obj R) :=
+      comp_preservesColimitsOfShape _ _
+    -- The two functors named below are the same functor.  `SSet.chainComplexFunctor C` is
+    -- `X ↦ X ⋙ sigmaConst.obj R` postcomposed with `alternatingFaceMapComplex`, and degree `n`
+    -- of an alternating face map complex is evaluation at `⦋n⦌`, on morphisms as well as on
+    -- objects; Mathlib records both halves of that as `rfl`, in `alternatingFaceMapComplex_obj_X`
+    -- and `alternatingFaceMapComplex_map_f`.  The comparison therefore has no content beyond the
+    -- identity, and no interface lemma can stand in for `Iso.refl` here; the `show` spells out
+    -- which two functors are being identified.
+    exact preservesColimitsOfShape_of_natIso
+      (show (evaluation SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ (Type w)).obj (Opposite.op ⦋n⦌) ⋙ sigmaConst.obj R ≅
+        (SSet.chainComplexFunctor.{w} C).obj R ⋙ HomologicalComplex.eval C _ n from Iso.refl _)
+
+end TauCeti
+
+namespace SSet
+
+variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasCoproducts.{w} C] [Preadditive C]
+  {X Y : SSet.{w}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (R : C)
+
+/-- The chain map induced by a monomorphism of simplicial sets is a monomorphism. -/
+instance mono_chainComplexMap [Mono f] : Mono (chainComplexMap f R) :=
+  HomologicalComplex.mono_of_mono_f _ fun _ ↦
+    inferInstanceAs (Mono ((sigmaConst.obj R).map (f.app _)))
+
+end SSet

+# The Mayer–Vietoris sequence of a pushout of simplicial sets
+
+Consider a commutative square of simplicial sets
+```
+     t
+ X₁  ⟶  X₂
+l|       |r
+ v       v
+ X₃  ⟶  X₄
+     b
+```
+and an object `R` of an abelian category with coproducts. Its Mayer–Vietoris short complex of
+chain complexes is `C(X₁; R) ⟶ C(X₂; R) ⊞ C(X₃; R) ⟶ C(X₄; R)`, with first map `(t, -l)` and
+second map `r + b`. When the square is a pushout and `t` is a monomorphism, this short complex is
+short exact: the chain complex functor preserves pushouts, and a pushout square in an abelian
+category is right exact in this form. The homology sequence of this short exact sequence is the
+Mayer–Vietoris long exact sequence
+`⋯ ⟶ Hₙ(X₁) ⟶ Hₙ(X₂) ⊞ Hₙ(X₃) ⟶ Hₙ(X₄) ⟶ Hₙ₋₁(X₁) ⟶ ⋯`,
+whose first two maps are `(t_*, -l_*)` and `r_* + b_*`.
+
+The typical pushout square is that of two subcomplexes `A` and `B` of a simplicial set, their
+intersection and their union (`SSet.Subcomplex.BicartSq.isPushout`). The Mayer–Vietoris sequence
+of singular homology for an open cover by two sets is obtained from such a square.
+
+## Main definitions and results
+
+* `SSet.shortExact_mayerVietorisShortComplex`: it is short exact for a pushout square whose top
+  map is a monomorphism; `SSet.shortExact_mayerVietoris` writes it with middle term
+  `C(X₂) ⊞ C(X₃)`, and its first map is split in each degree
+  (`SSet.isSplitMono_biprod_lift_chainComplexMap_f`).
+* `SSet.mayerVietorisToBiprod`, `SSet.mayerVietorisFromBiprod`: the maps
+  `Hₙ(X₁) ⟶ Hₙ(X₂) ⊞ Hₙ(X₃)` and `Hₙ(X₂) ⊞ Hₙ(X₃) ⟶ Hₙ(X₄)`.
+* `SSet.mayerVietorisδ`: the connecting morphism `Hₙ(X₄) ⟶ Hₘ(X₁)` for `m + 1 = n`.
+* `SSet.mayerVietoris_exact₁`, `SSet.mayerVietoris_exact₂`, `SSet.mayerVietoris_exact₃`:
+  exactness at `Hₘ(X₁)`, at `Hₙ(X₂) ⊞ Hₙ(X₃)` and at `Hₙ(X₄)`.
+* `SSet.epi_mayerVietorisFromBiprod_zero`: surjectivity at the degree-zero endpoint.
+* `SSet.mayerVietorisδ_naturality`: the connecting morphism is natural in maps of pushout squares.
+
+## References
+
+* A. Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Section 2.2, the Mayer–Vietoris sequences.
+-/

+
+variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasCoproducts.{w} C] [Abelian C] (R : C)
+  {X₁ X₂ X₃ X₄ : SSet.{w}} {t : X₁ ⟶ X₂} {l : X₁ ⟶ X₃} {r : X₂ ⟶ X₄} {b : X₃ ⟶ X₄}
+
+/-- **The Mayer–Vietoris short exact sequence of chain complexes.** For a pushout square of
+simplicial sets whose top map is a monomorphism, the Mayer–Vietoris short complex is short
+exact. -/
+lemma shortExact_mayerVietorisShortComplex (sq : IsPushout t l r b) [Mono t] :
+    (sq.map ((chainComplexFunctor C).obj R)).shortComplex.ShortExact where
+  -- The chain complex functor preserves pushouts.
+  exact := (sq.map ((chainComplexFunctor C).obj R)).exact_shortComplex
+  mono_f := by
+    -- Expose the chain map before typeclass synthesis of its mono instance.
+    change Mono (biprod.lift (chainComplexMap t R) (-chainComplexMap l R))
+    have : Mono (chainComplexMap t R) := inferInstance
+    exact mono_of_mono_fac (biprod.lift_fst (chainComplexMap t R) (-chainComplexMap l R))
+  epi_g := (sq.map ((chainComplexFunctor C).obj R)).epi_shortComplex_g
+
+/-! ### The long exact sequence -/
+
+/-- The first map `Hₙ(X₁) ⟶ Hₙ(X₂) ⊞ Hₙ(X₃)` of the Mayer–Vietoris sequence, with components
+`t_*` and `-l_*`. -/
+def mayerVietorisToBiprod (t : X₁ ⟶ X₂) (l : X₁ ⟶ X₃) (n : ℕ) :
+    X₁.homology R n ⟶ X₂.homology R n ⊞ X₃.homology R n :=
+  biprod.lift (SSet.homologyMap t R n) (-SSet.homologyMap l R n)
+
+@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
+lemma mayerVietorisToBiprod_fst (t : X₁ ⟶ X₂) (l : X₁ ⟶ X₃) (n : ℕ) :
+    mayerVietorisToBiprod R t l n ≫ biprod.fst = SSet.homologyMap t R n :=
+  biprod.lift_fst _ _
+
+@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
+lemma mayerVietorisToBiprod_snd (t : X₁ ⟶ X₂) (l : X₁ ⟶ X₃) (n : ℕ) :
+    mayerVietorisToBiprod R t l n ≫ biprod.snd = -SSet.homologyMap l R n :=
+  biprod.lift_snd _ _
+
+/-- The second map `Hₙ(X₂) ⊞ Hₙ(X₃) ⟶ Hₙ(X₄)` of the Mayer–Vietoris sequence, the sum of `r_*`
+and `b_*`. -/
+def mayerVietorisFromBiprod (r : X₂ ⟶ X₄) (b : X₃ ⟶ X₄) (n : ℕ) :
+    X₂.homology R n ⊞ X₃.homology R n ⟶ X₄.homology R n :=
+  biprod.desc (SSet.homologyMap r R n) (SSet.homologyMap b R n)
+
+@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
+lemma inl_mayerVietorisFromBiprod (r : X₂ ⟶ X₄) (b : X₃ ⟶ X₄) (n : ℕ) :
+    biprod.inl ≫ mayerVietorisFromBiprod R r b n = SSet.homologyMap r R n :=
+  biprod.inl_desc _ _
+
+@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
+lemma inr_mayerVietorisFromBiprod (r : X₂ ⟶ X₄) (b : X₃ ⟶ X₄) (n : ℕ) :
+    biprod.inr ≫ mayerVietorisFromBiprod R r b n = SSet.homologyMap b R n :=
+  biprod.inr_desc _ _
+
+@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
+lemma mayerVietorisToBiprod_fromBiprod (sq : CommSq t l r b) (n : ℕ) :
+    mayerVietorisToBiprod R t l n ≫ mayerVietorisFromBiprod R r b n = 0 := by
+  simp [mayerVietorisToBiprod, mayerVietorisFromBiprod, ← homologyMap_comp, sq.w]
+
+variable {Y₁ Y₂ Y₃ Y₄ : SSet.{w}} {t' : Y₁ ⟶ Y₂} {l' : Y₁ ⟶ Y₃} {r' : Y₂ ⟶ Y₄} {b' : Y₃ ⟶ Y₄}
+  (φ₁ : X₁ ⟶ Y₁) (φ₂ : X₂ ⟶ Y₂) (φ₃ : X₃ ⟶ Y₃) (φ₄ : X₄ ⟶ Y₄)
+
+/-- The first map of the Mayer–Vietoris sequence is natural in maps of squares. -/
+@[reassoc]
+lemma mayerVietorisToBiprod_naturality (ht : t ≫ φ₂ = φ₁ ≫ t') (hl : l ≫ φ₃ = φ₁ ≫ l')
+    (n : ℕ) :
+    mayerVietorisToBiprod R t l n ≫ biprod.map (SSet.homologyMap φ₂ R n) (SSet.homologyMap φ₃ R n) =
+      SSet.homologyMap φ₁ R n ≫ mayerVietorisToBiprod R t' l' n := by
+  ext <;> simp [← homologyMap_comp, ht, hl]
+
+/-- The second map of the Mayer–Vietoris sequence is natural in maps of squares. -/
+@[reassoc]
+lemma mayerVietorisFromBiprod_naturality (hr : r ≫ φ₄ = φ₂ ≫ r') (hb : b ≫ φ₄ = φ₃ ≫ b')
+    (n : ℕ) :
+    mayerVietorisFromBiprod R r b n ≫ SSet.homologyMap φ₄ R n =
+      biprod.map (SSet.homologyMap φ₂ R n) (SSet.homologyMap φ₃ R n) ≫
+        mayerVietorisFromBiprod R r' b' n := by
+  ext <;> simp [← homologyMap_comp, hr, hb]
+
+private lemma mayerVietorisToBiprod_eq (t : X₁ ⟶ X₂) (l : X₁ ⟶ X₃) (n : ℕ) :
+    mayerVietorisToBiprod R t l n =
+      biprod.lift (SSet.homologyMap t R n)
+        (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (-chainComplexMap l R) n) := by
+  rw [mayerVietorisToBiprod, HomologicalComplex.homologyMap_neg]
+
+/-- In each degree, the first map `C(X₁) ⟶ C(X₂) ⊞ C(X₃)` of the Mayer–Vietoris sequence is a split
+monomorphism when `t` is a monomorphism. -/
+instance isSplitMono_biprod_lift_chainComplexMap_f [Mono t] (i : ℕ) :
+    IsSplitMono ((biprod.lift (chainComplexMap t R) (-chainComplexMap l R)).f i) := by
+  -- `SSetPair.of t` has `t` as its structure map, so this is the split monomorphism instance for
+  -- the chains of a pair of simplicial sets.
+  have : IsSplitMono ((chainComplexMap t R).f i) :=
+    inferInstanceAs (IsSplitMono ((chainComplexMap (SSetPair.of t).hom R).f i))
+  exact IsSplitMono.mk'
+    { retraction := (biprod.fst : X₂.chainComplex R ⊞ X₃.chainComplex R ⟶ _).f i ≫
+        retraction ((chainComplexMap t R).f i)
+      id := by rw [← Category.assoc, ← HomologicalComplex.comp_f, biprod.lift_fst,
+        IsSplitMono.id] }
+
+variable (sq : IsPushout t l r b) [Mono t]
+
+/-- The Mayer–Vietoris short exact sequence, written with its middle term `C(X₂) ⊞ C(X₃)`. -/
+lemma shortExact_mayerVietoris :
+    (ShortComplex.mk (biprod.lift (chainComplexMap t R) (-chainComplexMap l R))
+      (biprod.desc (chainComplexMap r R) (chainComplexMap b R))
+      (sq.map ((chainComplexFunctor C).obj R)).shortComplex.zero).ShortExact :=
+  shortExact_mayerVietorisShortComplex R sq
+
+/-- The Mayer–Vietoris connecting morphism `Hₙ(X₄) ⟶ Hₘ(X₁)`, where `m + 1 = n`: the connecting
+morphism of the Mayer–Vietoris short exact sequence of chain complexes. -/
+def mayerVietorisδ (n m : ℕ) (h : m + 1 = n := by lia) : X₄.homology R n ⟶ X₁.homology R m :=
+  (shortExact_mayerVietorisShortComplex R sq).δ n m h
+
+lemma mayerVietorisδ_def (n m : ℕ) (h : m + 1 = n := by lia) :
+    mayerVietorisδ R sq n m h = (shortExact_mayerVietorisShortComplex R sq).δ n m h := (rfl)
+
+@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
+lemma mayerVietorisδ_toBiprod (n m : ℕ) (h : m + 1 = n := by lia) :
+    mayerVietorisδ R sq n m h ≫ mayerVietorisToBiprod R t l m = 0 := by
+  rw [mayerVietorisToBiprod_eq]
+  exact (shortExact_mayerVietoris R sq).δ_comp_biprod_lift_homologyMap n m h
+
+@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
+lemma mayerVietorisFromBiprod_δ (n m : ℕ) (h : m + 1 = n := by lia) :
+    mayerVietorisFromBiprod R r b n ≫ mayerVietorisδ R sq n m h = 0 :=
+  (shortExact_mayerVietoris R sq).biprod_desc_homologyMap_comp_δ n m h
+
+/-- **Exactness of the Mayer–Vietoris sequence at `Hₘ(X₁)`.** -/
+lemma mayerVietoris_exact₁ (n m : ℕ) (h : m + 1 = n := by lia) :
+    (ShortComplex.mk _ _ (mayerVietorisδ_toBiprod R sq n m h)).Exact := by
+  convert (shortExact_mayerVietoris R sq).biprod_homology_exact₁ n m h using 2
+  exacts [rfl, mayerVietorisToBiprod_eq R t l m]
+
+/-- **Exactness of the Mayer–Vietoris sequence at `Hₙ(X₂) ⊞ Hₙ(X₃)`.** -/
+lemma mayerVietoris_exact₂ (n : ℕ) :
+    (ShortComplex.mk _ _ (mayerVietorisToBiprod_fromBiprod R sq.toCommSq n)).Exact := by
+  convert (shortExact_mayerVietoris R sq).biprod_homology_exact₂ n using 2
+  exacts [mayerVietorisToBiprod_eq R t l n, rfl]
+
+/-- **Exactness of the Mayer–Vietoris sequence at `Hₙ(X₄)`.** -/
+lemma mayerVietoris_exact₃ (n m : ℕ) (h : m + 1 = n := by lia) :
+    (ShortComplex.mk _ _ (mayerVietorisFromBiprod_δ R sq n m h)).Exact :=
+  (shortExact_mayerVietoris R sq).biprod_homology_exact₃ n m h
+
+include sq in
+/-- The map `H₀(X₂) ⊞ H₀(X₃) ⟶ H₀(X₄)` at the end of the Mayer–Vietoris sequence is an
+epimorphism. -/
+lemma epi_mayerVietorisFromBiprod_zero : Epi (mayerVietorisFromBiprod R r b 0) := by
+  have : Epi ((biprod.desc (chainComplexMap r R) (chainComplexMap b R)).f 0) :=
+    ((HomologicalComplex.shortExact_iff_degreewise_shortExact _).1
+      (shortExact_mayerVietorisShortComplex R sq) 0).epi_g
+  have : Epi (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
+      (biprod.desc (chainComplexMap r R) (chainComplexMap b R)) 0) :=
+    HomologicalComplex.epi_homologyMap_of_epi_of_not_rel _ _ (by simp)
+  exact HomologicalComplex.epi_biprod_desc_homologyMap 0
+
+/-- **Naturality of the Mayer–Vietoris connecting morphism** in maps of pushout squares. -/
+@[reassoc]
+lemma mayerVietorisδ_naturality (sq' : IsPushout t' l' r' b') [Mono t']
+    (ht : t ≫ φ₂ = φ₁ ≫ t') (hl : l ≫ φ₃ = φ₁ ≫ l') (hr : r ≫ φ₄ = φ₂ ≫ r')
+    (hb : b ≫ φ₄ = φ₃ ≫ b') (n m : ℕ) (h : m + 1 = n := by lia) :
+    mayerVietorisδ R sq n m h ≫ SSet.homologyMap φ₁ R m =
+      SSet.homologyMap φ₄ R n ≫ mayerVietorisδ R sq' n m h := by
+  let ψ : (sq.map ((chainComplexFunctor C).obj R)).shortComplex ⟶
+      (sq'.map ((chainComplexFunctor C).obj R)).shortComplex :=
+    { τ₁ := chainComplexMap φ₁ R
+      τ₂ := biprod.map (chainComplexMap φ₂ R) (chainComplexMap φ₃ R)
+      τ₃ := chainComplexMap φ₄ R
+      comm₁₂ := by
+        -- Expose the two `f` maps to check the square on both biproduct projections.
+        change chainComplexMap φ₁ R ≫
+            biprod.lift (chainComplexMap t' R) (-chainComplexMap l' R) =
+          biprod.lift (chainComplexMap t R) (-chainComplexMap l R) ≫
+            biprod.map (chainComplexMap φ₂ R) (chainComplexMap φ₃ R)
+        apply biprod.hom_ext <;> simp [← Functor.map_comp, ht, hl]
+      comm₂₃ := by
+        -- Expose the two `g` maps to check the square on both biproduct inclusions.
+        change biprod.map (chainComplexMap φ₂ R) (chainComplexMap φ₃ R) ≫
+            biprod.desc (chainComplexMap r' R) (chainComplexMap b' R) =
+          biprod.desc (chainComplexMap r R) (chainComplexMap b R) ≫ chainComplexMap φ₄ R
+        apply biprod.hom_ext' <;> simp [← Functor.map_comp, hr, hb] }
+  exact HomologicalComplex.HomologySequence.δ_naturality ψ _ _ n m h
+
+end SSet
